title: Vendor Signal Cartography and Cost-Sensitivity Study for Model Fallbacks
creator: Maya Hart
description:
Objective: produce an operational map of vendor/model signals (availability, price/latency tiers, quantization support, legal/licensing notes) and run cohort-level cost-sensitivity simulations to inform automated fallback policies and Dedicated capacity procurement triggers.

Scope: inventory 12 high-priority model families across 4 vendor sources (public open weights, hosted vendors, third-party mirrors, internal verified variants). For each model-vendor pair capture: region availability, quant formats supported, typical token latency at 512/2048 tokens on common GPU classes, per-token published cost (or estimated $/1k tokens), license restrictions (commercial/derivative clauses), and observed stability incidents in the past 90 days.

Approach: 1) Data collection sprint: run synthetic inference benchmarks (512/2048 tokens) on sample inputs in eu-west-1 and us-west-2; record tail latency and cost estimates. 2) License/legal triage: summarize S3-level licensing constraints for enterprise fallback suitability. 3) Cost-sensitivity cohort modeling: using three customer workload cohorts (chat-high-turn, embeddings-batch, summary-long-form) simulate substitution scenarios with realistic traffic shapes and batching/caching enabled. 4) Produce a vendor-signal cartography visual and a ranked list of safe fallback candidates by cohort with trigger thresholds for automatic fallback (latency budget breach, capacity exhaustion, price surge).

Deliverables: - Vendor signal cartography dashboard (spreadsheet + one-page visual) describing trade-offs per vendor/model. - Cohort cost-sensitivity workbook with scenario outputs and recommended fallback trigger values. - Actionable runbook for runtime and console teams: JSON snippets for fallback policy thresholds, recommended Dedicated capacity sizing per cohort, and an incident playbook for vendor outages. - Short PRD for a follow-up feature: automated fallback tester (end-to-end canary that validates fallbacks monthly).

Success criteria: - Cartography covers >=90% of current active customer consumption (by token volume). - Cost-sensitivity runs produce clear recommended fallback thresholds for each cohort and identify at least two fallback candidates per primary model with low legal friction. - Runtime team can ingest the recommended thresholds into canary policies with <=2 engineering workdays of integration effort.

Risks and trade-offs: - Public cost estimates are noisy; we will triangulate with live benchmarks but accept an error margin. - Licensing ambiguity may force conservative fallback choices; legal review could delay final recommendations. - Representative traffic shapes must be derived from sampled telemetry; privacy-preserving aggregation needed for customer cohorts.

Stakeholders: Product (Maya Hart), Runtime/Serving (Diego Morales, Priya Nair), Research (Rui Zhang), Legal (Anita Kapoor), Console (Luis Ortega).
